senses.en: a chemical substance that is present at the start of a chemical reaction

examples.text: In the experiment, the students measured how quickly each reactant was consumed as the temperature rose.

senses.en: opposed to political or social liberalism or reform

examples.text: The reactionary government banned unions and censored newspapers to block any demand for reform.

senses.en: an extreme conservative; an opponent of progress or liberalism

examples.text: Progressives accused the reactionaries in parliament of trying to restore the privileges of the old aristocracy.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 réactionnaire에서 왔습니다. 프랑스 혁명에 맞서 반작용을 일으키려던 사람을 가리켰습니다.

senses.en: the act of adjusting again (to changed circumstances)

examples.text: Returning veterans faced a difficult readjustment to civilian life after years of service overseas.

senses.en: To obtain or receive as a reward, in a good or a bad sense.

examples.text: Companies that invested early in research are now reaping the rewards of their patience.

senses.en: gather, as of natural products

examples.text: Farmers gathered at dawn to reap the wheat before the autumn rains arrived.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 rēopan('베다')에서 왔습니다. 곡식을 베어 거두듯 결과를 거둔다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To criticise harshly; to reprove.

examples.text: The judge sharply rebuked the lawyer for repeatedly interrupting the witness during testimony.

senses.en: an act or expression of criticism and censure

examples.text: The senator's speech was a stinging rebuke of the administration's foreign policy.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 buchier('치다, 쪼개다')에 re-가 붙은 말입니다. 되받아 두들긴다는 데서 꾸짖는다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a puzzle where you decode a message consisting of pictures representing syllables and words

examples.text: The children solved the rebus by recognizing that a picture of an eye and a sea meant 'I see'.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rēbus('사물들로')에서 온 프랑스어에서 왔습니다. 글자 대신 사물 그림으로 말을 나타내는 수수께끼입니다.

senses.en: prove to be false or incorrect

examples.text: The defense attorney rebutted the prosecution's claims with documents showing her client was abroad that night.

senses.en: To deny the truth of something, especially by presenting arguments that disprove it.

examples.text: The company issued a statement rebutting allegations that it had concealed safety data.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reboter('되밀치다')에서 왔고 butt('들이받다')와 이어집니다. 상대 주장을 되받아 밀쳐 냅니다.

senses.en: stubbornly resistant to authority or control
senses.ko: 고집 세고 말을 안 듣는, 반항적인

examples.text: The recalcitrant board members refused to approve the merger despite weeks of persuasion.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recalcitrāre('뒤로 걷어차다')에서 왔고 calx('발뒤꿈치')가 어원입니다. 말이 뒷발질하듯 반항합니다.

senses.en: formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure

examples.text: Under threat of imprisonment, the astronomer was forced to recant his claim that the earth moved.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recantāre('다시 노래하다, 취소하다')에서 왔습니다. 이미 부른 노래를 거꾸로 부르듯 앞말을 철회합니다.

senses.en: summarize briefly

examples.text: Before taking questions, the lecturer recapitulated the main arguments of the previous three sessions.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 recapitulāre에서 왔습니다. capitulum('머리, 요점')을 다시 짚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a summary at the end that repeats the substance of a longer discussion

examples.text: The final chapter offers a brief recapitulation of the book's central claims for hurried readers.

senses.en: (music) the section of a composition or movement (especially in sonata form) in which musical themes that were introduced earlier are repeated

examples.text: In the recapitulation, the opening theme returns in the home key after a stormy development section.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 recapitulatio('요약')에서 왔습니다. 요점을 다시 짚어 되풀이하는 일입니다.

senses.en: one who lives in solitude

examples.text: After her husband died, the once-sociable author became a recluse and refused all interviews.

senses.en: withdrawn from society; seeking solitude

examples.text: lived an unsocial reclusive life

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reclus('가둬진')에서 왔고 라틴어 reclūdere에서 나왔습니다. 문을 닫아걸고 홀로 사는 사람입니다.

senses.en: make (one thing) compatible with (another)

examples.text: It is hard to reconcile the company's green slogans with its record of polluting nearby rivers.

senses.en: To restore a friendly relationship; to bring back or return to harmony.

examples.text: to reconcile people who have quarrelled

senses.en: accept as inevitable

examples.text: After years of appeals, she finally reconciled herself to the loss of the family farm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reconciliāre('다시 화해시키다')에서 왔습니다. 어긋난 것을 다시 맞춘다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge

examples.text: The journal publishes recondite essays on medieval logic that few readers outside the field can follow.

senses.en: Little known; esoteric, secret.

examples.text: Her recondite knowledge of obscure dialects made her an invaluable consultant for linguists.

senses.en: act of turning to for assistance

examples.text: have recourse to the courts

senses.en: something or someone turned to for assistance or security

examples.text: his only recourse was the police

origin.ko: 라틴어 recursus('되달려옴')에서 왔습니다. 도움을 구해 되돌아가 달려간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: returning to health after illness or debility

examples.text: The recovering patient was advised to rest for several weeks before returning to work.

senses.en: mutual accusations

examples.text: The peace talks collapsed amid bitter recriminations over who had broken the ceasefire.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 récrimination에서 왔습니다. 비난을 되받아 되돌려 서로 맞고발하는 일입니다.

senses.en: To recur, or break out anew after a quiescence or dormant period.

examples.text: Old tensions between the two communities recrudesced after the election, ending years of calm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recrūdēscere('다시 날것이 되다')의 영향을 받은 말입니다. 아물던 상처가 다시 도지듯 재발한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Breaking out again or reemerging after temporary abatement or suppression.

examples.text: Officials feared a recrudescent wave of violence once the troops withdrew from the region.

origin.ko: 라틴어 recrūdēscō('다시 날것이 되다')에서 왔습니다. 가라앉았던 상처가 다시 생생해져 도집니다.

senses.en: serving to bring to mind

examples.text: The film's soft colors and jazz score are redolent of postwar Paris.

senses.en: (used with ‘of’ or ‘with’) noticeably odorous

examples.text: the hall was redolent of floor wax

origin.ko: 라틴어 redolēre('냄새를 풍기다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 냄새가 기억을 불러내듯 무언가를 연상시킵니다.

senses.en: inspiring fear

examples.text: The challenger faced a redoubtable opponent who had not lost a debate in ten years.

senses.en: worthy of respect or honor

examples.text: born of a redoubtable family

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 redoter('두려워하다')에 -able이 붙은 말입니다. 두려워할 만한 상대라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: have an effect for good or ill

examples.text: Her efforts will redound to the general good

senses.en: To contribute to the honour, shame etc. of a person or organisation.

examples.text: The scandal will redound to the discredit of everyone who tried to hide the facts.

origin.ko: 라틴어 redundāre('넘쳐 흐르다')에서 왔고 unda('물결')가 어원입니다. 파도가 되돌아오듯 결과가 돌아옵니다.

senses.en: make reparations or amends for

examples.text: The government pledged to redress the injustices suffered by families displaced during the dam project.

senses.en: act of correcting an error or a fault or an evil

examples.text: Workers who were unfairly dismissed sought redress through the labor tribunal.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 redrecier('다시 세우다')에서 왔습니다. 쓰러진 것을 바로 세우듯 잘못을 바로잡고 보상한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a communal dining-hall (usually in a monastery)

examples.text: The monks gathered in the refectory each evening for a silent meal.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 refectorium에서 왔고 reficere('다시 만들다')에서 나왔습니다. 먹고 기운을 되찾는 식당입니다.

senses.en: improve or perfect by pruning or polishing

examples.text: refine one's style of writing

senses.en: reduce to a fine, unmixed, or pure state; separate from extraneous matter or cleanse from impurities

examples.text: refine sugar

senses.en: reflect deeply on a subject

examples.text: Before replying, she paused to reflect on what the committee's criticism really meant.

senses.en: give evidence of the quality of

examples.text: The mess in his dorm room reflects on the student

senses.en: to throw or bend back (from a surface)

examples.text: Sound is reflected well in this auditorium

origin.ko: 라틴어 reflectere('뒤로 구부리다')에서 왔습니다. 빛을 되꺾어 비추듯 생각을 되돌려 숙고한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: stubbornly resistant to authority or control

examples.text: The refractory mule balked at every command and would not pull the cart up the hill.

senses.en: not responding to treatment

examples.text: Doctors tried three antibiotics before concluding the infection was refractory to standard treatment.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refractārius('고집 센')에서 왔고 refringere('부수다')와 이어집니다. 꺾이지 않고 버티는 고집입니다.

senses.en: radiating or as if radiating light

examples.text: The refulgent dome of the cathedral glowed in the late afternoon sun.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refulgēre('되비쳐 빛나다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 눈부시게 빛을 내뿜는 모습입니다.

senses.en: prove to be false or incorrect

examples.text: New archaeological evidence refuted the long-held theory that the settlement was abandoned suddenly.

origin.ko: 라틴어 refūtāre('물리치다, 반박하다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: go back to a previous state

examples.text: Under stress, the toddler began to regress, refusing to walk and demanding to be carried.

senses.en: returning to a former state

examples.text: Critics saw the new policy as a regress to the discredited practices of an earlier era.

origin.ko: 라틴어 regredī('되돌아가다')에서 왔습니다. 뒤로 걸어 이전 상태로 간다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: to say, state, or perform again

examples.text: The spokesman reiterated that the government would not negotiate with the kidnappers under any circumstances.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 reiterāre('되풀이하다')에서 왔고 iterum('다시')에서 나왔습니다. 같은 말을 다시 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)

examples.text: it brought a sharp rejoinder from the teacher

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rejoindre('다시 잇다')의 부정사를 명사로 쓴 말입니다. 상대 말에 되받아 이어 응답하는 것입니다.

senses.en: assign to a lower position; reduce in rank

examples.text: The once-celebrated director was relegated to making low-budget commercials after a string of failures.

senses.en: refer to another person for decision or judgment

examples.text: She likes to relegate difficult questions to her colleagues

origin.ko: 라틴어 relēgāre('쫓아 보내다, 추방하다')에서 왔습니다. 뒤로 밀어 보낸다는 데서 '강등시키다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To give in or be swayed; to become less hard, harsh, or cruel; to show clemency.

examples.text: After weeks of protest, the mayor finally relented and agreed to reopen the community pool.

senses.en: To slacken; to abate.

examples.text: We waited for the storm to relent before we ventured outside.

origin.ko: 라틴어 lentus('부드러운, 유연한')에서 나온 말입니다. 굳은 마음이 다시 부드러워져 누그러진다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: part with a possession or right

examples.text: The aging founder was reluctant to relinquish control of the company to his younger daughter.

senses.en: release, as from one's grip

examples.text: The climber slowly relinquished his grip on the rope as the rescuers took his weight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 relinquere('뒤에 남기고 떠나다')에서 왔습니다. 가진 것을 두고 떠나 포기한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: derive or receive pleasure from; get enjoyment from; take pleasure in

examples.text: She relished her fame and basked in her glory

senses.en: vigorous and enthusiastic enjoyment

examples.text: The debater attacked her opponent's argument with obvious relish, delighting the crowd.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reles('남은 것')에서 나온 release('냄새, 맛')의 변형입니다. 맛을 음미한다는 데서 '즐기다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: tending or intended to rectify or improve

examples.text: a remedial reading course

senses.en: tending to cure or restore to health

examples.text: The spa advertised the remedial properties of its mineral springs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remediālis에서 왔으며 remedy('치료')에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 부족한 것을 고쳐 주는 교육 등에 씁니다.

senses.en: failing in what duty requires

examples.text: It would be remiss of the committee to ignore the warnings raised by the auditors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remissus('느슨해진, 게으른')에서 왔고 remittere('늦추다')의 과거분사입니다. 조여 둘 의무가 느슨해진 상태입니다.

senses.en: an abatement in intensity or degree (as in the manifestations of a disease)

examples.text: his cancer is in remission

senses.en: A pardon of a sin; (chiefly historical, also figuratively) the forgiveness of an offence, or relinquishment of a (legal) claim or a debt.

examples.text: The ancient ritual promised remission of sins to all who made the pilgrimage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remissiō에서 왔고 remittere('늦추어 보내다')와 이어집니다. 병세를 풀어 늦춘다는 '완화'입니다.

senses.en: argue in protest or opposition

examples.text: Parents gathered at the school to remonstrate with the board over the planned closure.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 remōnstrāre에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 되받아 지적해 보여 주며 항의한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unlikely to occur

examples.text: Analysts said there was only a remote chance that the two rivals would agree to merge.

senses.en: Emotionally detached.

examples.text: After the divorce, he grew remote and rarely spoke to his colleagues at lunch.

origin.ko: 라틴어 remōtus('멀리 치워진')에서 왔고 removēre('치우다')의 과거분사입니다. 멀리 떨어져 가능성이 희박하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the act of paying for goods or services or to recompense for losses

examples.text: adequate remuneration for his work

origin.ko: 라틴어 remūnerātiō에서 왔습니다. munus('선물, 의무')를 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tear or be torn violently

examples.text: The violent storm threatened to rend the old sail into ribbons before the ship reached harbor.

senses.en: To violently disturb the peace of; to throw into chaos.

examples.text: A bitter dispute over succession threatened to rend the royal family apart.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 rendan('찢다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: cause to become

examples.text: The shot rendered her immobile

senses.en: pass down

examples.text: render a verdict

senses.en: give an interpretation or rendition of

examples.text: The pianist rendered the Beethoven sonata beautifully

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rendre('되돌려 주다')에서 왔고 라틴어 reddere에서 나왔습니다. 어떤 상태로 되돌려 놓는다는 데서 '~하게 만들다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: a disloyal person who betrays or deserts their cause or religion or political party or friend etc.

examples.text: The party denounced him as a renegade after he voted with the opposition on every key issue.

senses.en: Unconventional, unorthodox.

examples.text: The renegade physicist published theories that defied nearly every assumption of his field.

origin.ko: 스페인어 renegado에서 왔고 라틴어 renegāre('부인하다')에서 나왔습니다. 믿음을 저버린 배신자입니다.

senses.en: fail to fulfill a promise or obligation

examples.text: she reneged on her promise

origin.ko: 라틴어 renegāre('부인하다')에서 왔습니다. 했던 약속을 부인하고 어긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: give up, such as power, as of monarchs and emperors, or duties and obligations

examples.text: The prince renounced his claim to the throne in order to marry a commoner.

senses.en: cast off

examples.text: She renounced her husband

origin.ko: 라틴어 renūntiāre('거절을 알리다')에서 왔습니다. 가진 권리를 내려놓겠다고 공식으로 알리는 것입니다.

senses.en: the food served and eaten at one time

examples.text: After the long journey, the travelers sat down to a modest but welcome repast.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 repastus('식사')에서 왔고 repāscere('먹이다')와 이어집니다. 기운을 되찾게 해 주는 한 끼입니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: Parliament voted to repeal the outdated law that had restricted public gatherings for decades.

senses.en: the act of abrogating; an official or legal cancellation

examples.text: Lawmakers voted for the repeal of the unpopular tax after months of public pressure.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 rapeler('불러들이다, 철회하다')에서 왔고 라틴어 repellere와 이어집니다. 이미 내린 법을 거두어들입니다.

senses.en: a remote or indirect consequence of some action

examples.text: his declaration had unforeseen repercussions

origin.ko: 라틴어 repercutere('되튀게 하다')에서 왔습니다. 쳤을 때 되돌아오는 반향이 '간접적 영향'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: the entire range of skills or aptitudes or devices used in a particular field or occupation

examples.text: The negotiator's repertoire of tactics ranged from patient listening to calculated silence.

senses.en: a collection of works (plays, songs, operas, ballets) that an artist or company can perform and do perform for short intervals on a regular schedule

examples.text: The opera company's repertoire includes works by Mozart and Verdi.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 repertōrium('목록, 재고')에서 온 프랑스어를 빌려 왔습니다. 공연할 수 있는 작품 목록을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: express discontent

examples.text: Rather than repine over his lost fortune, he set about rebuilding his business from nothing.

origin.ko: re-에 pine('애타게 그리워하다')을 붙여 만든 것으로 보입니다. 마음이 상해 불평한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: fill something that had previously been emptied

examples.text: The charity worked to replenish the food bank's shelves before the winter holidays.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 replenir('다시 채우다')에서 왔고 라틴어 plenus('가득한')가 어원입니다.

senses.en: (followed by ‘with’) deeply filled or permeated

examples.text: The memoir is replete with vivid details of life in a wartime village.

senses.en: filled to satisfaction with food or drink

examples.text: After the holiday feast, the guests lay replete and drowsy on the sofas.

origin.ko: 라틴어 repletus('가득 채워진')에서 왔습니다. 속이 꽉 찬 상태입니다.

senses.en: freedom from activity (work or strain or responsibility)

examples.text: took his repose by the swimming pool

senses.en: a disposition free from stress or emotion

examples.text: Even in the middle of the crisis, the old judge maintained an air of calm repose.

senses.en: lean in a comfortable resting position

examples.text: He was reposing on the couch

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reposer('쉬다')에서 왔고 후기 라틴어 repausāre('쉬게 하다')와 이어집니다. 몸을 내려놓고 쉬는 안식입니다.

senses.en: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure

examples.text: The council condemned the contractor's reprehensible decision to ignore basic safety rules.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 reprehensibilis에서 왔고 reprehendere('붙잡아 꾸짖다')와 이어집니다. 꾸짖어 마땅하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An act of retaliation.

examples.text: Villagers feared reprisals if they cooperated with the investigators, so few agreed to testify.

origin.ko: 고대 이탈리아어 ripresaglia에서 왔고 riprendere('되찾아 가다')와 이어집니다. 당한 만큼 되가져오는 보복입니다.

senses.en: A repetition of a phrase, a return to an earlier theme, or a second rendition or version of a song in a programme or musical.

examples.text: The film ends with a quiet reprise of the melody that opened the first scene.

senses.en: A recurrence or resumption of an action.

examples.text: The senator's speech was a reprise of arguments she had made throughout the campaign.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reprendre('다시 잡다')에서 왔습니다. 앞의 주제를 다시 집어 드는 반복입니다.

senses.en: To criticize or rebuke (someone).

examples.text: She reproached herself for failing to notice the warning signs sooner.

senses.en: a mild rebuke or criticism

examples.text: words of reproach

senses.en: disgrace or shame

examples.text: he brought reproach upon his family

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 reprochier('나무라다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A person with low morals or principles.

examples.text: The village gossips called him a drunken reprobate who had squandered his family's fortune.

senses.en: deviating from what is considered moral or right or proper or good

examples.text: The preacher denounced the reprobate city and warned its citizens to mend their ways.

senses.en: express strong disapproval of

examples.text: Church leaders reprobated the spread of gambling dens near the harbor in a sharply worded letter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reprobātus('인정받지 못한')에서 왔습니다. 시험에서 불합격해 버림받은 타락한 사람입니다.

senses.en: severe disapproval

examples.text: The editorial met the minister's remarks with open reprobation and called for his resignation.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 réprobation 또는 라틴어 reprobatio에서 왔으며 reprobate에 -ion이 붙은 말입니다. 인정하지 않고 내치는 강한 비난입니다.

senses.en: reject as untrue, unfounded, or unjust

examples.text: She repudiated the accusations

senses.en: refuse to acknowledge, ratify, or recognize as valid

examples.text: The woman repudiated the divorce settlement

senses.en: To refuse to have any relation to; to disown.

examples.text: The movement publicly repudiated its founder after he praised violent extremists.

origin.ko: 라틴어 repudiāre('내치다')에서 왔고 repudium('거부, 이혼')와 이어집니다. 받아들이지 않고 물리친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Offensive or repulsive; arousing disgust or aversion.

examples.text: Most citizens found the regime's treatment of prisoners morally repugnant.

senses.en: Opposed or in conflict.

examples.text: a repugnant condition

origin.ko: 라틴어 repugnāre('맞서 싸우다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 마음이 맞서 싸울 만큼 불쾌하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make repayment for or return something

examples.text: He hoped one day to requite the kindness of the neighbors who had sheltered his family.

origin.ko: re-에 중세 영어 quiten('갚다')이 붙은 말입니다. 받은 것을 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: cancel officially

examples.text: The university rescinded its offer after discovering that the applicant had falsified her credentials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 rescindere('잘라 내다')에서 왔습니다. 이미 있는 것을 뒤로 잘라 없애 철회한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a statement that limits or restricts some claim

examples.text: he recommended her without any reservations

senses.en: an unstated doubt that prevents you from accepting something wholeheartedly

examples.text: Several members voiced private reservations about the plan even as they voted in its favor.

senses.en: a district that is reserved for particular purpose

examples.text: The tribe's reservation covers a large stretch of arid land in the northern part of the state.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 reservation에서 왔고 reserve('따로 간직하다')에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 일부를 따로 남겨 두는 단서입니다.

senses.en: An uncomplaining acceptance of something undesirable but unavoidable.

examples.text: She faced the diagnosis with quiet resignation, putting her affairs in order without complaint.

senses.en: the act of giving up (a claim or office or possession etc.)

examples.text: The minister's resignation followed weeks of mounting pressure over the budget scandal.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 resignātiō에서 왔고 resign('내놓다')에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 바꿀 수 없는 일을 그대로 받아들이는 체념입니다.

senses.en: recovering readily from adversity, depression, or the like

examples.text: Small businesses proved resilient during the downturn, adapting quickly to the sudden change in demand.

senses.en: elastic; rebounds readily

examples.text: Rubber is valued for being a resilient material that returns to its shape after stretching.

origin.ko: 라틴어 resilīre('뒤로 튀어 오르다')에서 왔습니다. 눌려도 도로 튀어 오르는 회복력입니다.

senses.en: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination

examples.text: stood resolute against the enemy

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolūtus('풀려난')에서 왔고 resolvere('풀다')의 과거분사입니다. 의문이 풀려 결심이 굳은 상태입니다.

senses.en: A strong will; the state of being resolute.

examples.text: The explorers faced the blizzard with a resolution that astonished even their own guides.

senses.en: finding a solution to a problem

examples.text: Both sides welcomed the swift resolution of the dispute over water rights.

senses.en: a formal expression by a meeting; agreed to by a vote

examples.text: The assembly passed a resolution condemning the use of chemical weapons.

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolūtiō('풀어냄')에서 왔습니다. 갈등을 풀고 마음을 굳히는 결의입니다.

senses.en: reach a decision

examples.text: he resolved never to drink again

senses.en: bring to an end; settle conclusively

examples.text: The mediator helped resolve the long dispute between the neighboring towns.

senses.en: the trait of being resolute

examples.text: his resoluteness carried him through the battle

origin.ko: 라틴어 resolvere('풀다, 녹이다')에서 왔습니다. 문제를 풀어 결론에 이르러 결심한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: serving to bring to mind

examples.text: The poem's simple images are resonant with memories of the poet's childhood.

senses.en: characterized by resonance

examples.text: a resonant voice

origin.ko: 라틴어 resonāre('다시 울리다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 마음에 메아리처럼 되울려 떠올리게 합니다.

senses.en: the ability to deal resourcefully with unusual problems

examples.text: a man of resource

senses.en: a source of aid or support that may be drawn upon when needed

examples.text: the local library is a valuable resource

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 resourdre('다시 솟아나다')에서 왔고 라틴어 resurgere와 이어집니다. 솟아나는 샘 같은 임기응변의 재주입니다.

senses.en: in the order given

examples.text: the brothers were called Felix and Max, respectively

senses.en: A brief interval of rest or relief.

examples.text: The rain brought a brief respite from the heat that had gripped the city for weeks.

senses.en: the act of reprieving; postponing or remitting punishment

examples.text: The governor granted the prisoner a respite hours before the scheduled execution.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 respit('휴식')에서 왔고 라틴어 respectus('뒤돌아봄')와 이어집니다. 잠시 멈추어 돌아보는 쉼입니다.

senses.en: impatient especially under restriction or delay

examples.text: The restive crowd began to jeer as the speaker's remarks dragged on past midnight.

senses.en: Resistant to control; stubborn.

examples.text: The restive provinces repeatedly defied orders from the central government.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 restif('멈춰 서 있는')에서 왔고 라틴어 restāre('머물다')와 이어집니다. 명령을 안 듣고 버티던 말에서 '안달하는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by avoidance of extravagance or extremes

examples.text: The prime minister gave a restrained response to the insult, avoiding any hint of anger.

senses.en: not showy or obtrusive

examples.text: The restrained decor of the hotel, in muted grays and creams, put guests instantly at ease.

senses.en: rising again as to new life and vigor

examples.text: resurgent nationalism

senses.en: a fee charged in advance to retain the services of someone

examples.text: The firm paid the consultant a monthly retainer to remain available for urgent questions.

senses.en: a person working in the service of another (especially in the household)

examples.text: The old retainer had served the family faithfully for more than forty years.

origin.ko: retain('붙들어 두다')에 -er가 붙은 말입니다. 전문가를 계속 붙들어 두려고 미리 내는 선임료입니다.

senses.en: take revenge for a perceived wrong

examples.text: The country threatened to retaliate with tariffs if the trade restrictions were not lifted.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retāliāre('똑같이 갚다')에서 왔습니다. 당한 만큼 되돌려 갚는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: good at remembering

examples.text: a retentive mind

senses.en: having the power, capacity, or quality of retaining water

examples.text: soils retentive of moisture

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 retentivus에서 왔고 라틴어 retentus('붙들린')와 이어집니다. 머릿속에 꽉 붙들어 두는 기억력입니다.

senses.en: temperamentally disinclined to talk

examples.text: The usually reticent scientist surprised everyone by speaking openly about her failed experiments.

senses.en: reluctant to draw attention to yourself

examples.text: Reticent about her achievements, she let her colleagues take most of the public credit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 reticēre('입을 다물다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 말을 아끼는 과묵함입니다.

senses.en: the group following and attending to some important person

examples.text: The ambassador arrived with a large retinue of aides, bodyguards, and translators.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 retenue('붙들어 둠')에서 왔고 retenir('붙들다')와 이어집니다. 높은 사람이 곁에 붙들어 두는 수행원입니다.

senses.en: reluctant to draw attention to yourself

examples.text: The retiring young scholar avoided public lectures and preferred the quiet of the archive.

senses.en: of a person who has held and relinquished a position or office

examples.text: a retiring member of the board

senses.en: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)

examples.text: Her witty retort to the heckler drew laughter and applause from the whole audience.

senses.en: answer back

examples.text: When accused of laziness, she retorted that nobody else had worked on the weekend.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retorquēre('뒤로 비틀다')에서 왔습니다. 상대 말을 되비틀어 받아치는 응수입니다.

senses.en: formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure

examples.text: He retracted his earlier statements about his religion

senses.en: pull inward or towards a center

examples.text: The snail slowly retracted its horns into its shell when the child touched the leaf.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retrahere('뒤로 끌다')에서 왔습니다. 내놓은 말을 도로 끌어당겨 철회한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tighten one's belt; use resources carefully

examples.text: Facing falling revenue, the university was forced to retrench and freeze all new hiring.

senses.en: make a reduction, as in one's workforce

examples.text: The company had to retrench

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 retranchier('잘라 내다')에서 왔습니다. 비용을 잘라 내 긴축한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: concerned with or related to the past

examples.text: The study took a retrospective approach, examining medical records from the previous twenty years.

senses.en: an exhibition of a representative selection of an artist's life work

examples.text: The museum's retrospective traced the painter's evolution from early portraits to late abstractions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 retrōspicere('뒤돌아보다')에서 왔습니다. 지나온 과거를 되돌아본다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To improve, renew, renovate, or revise (something).

examples.text: The airline plans to revamp its loyalty program to attract more frequent business travelers.

origin.ko: re-('다시')에 vamp('수선하다')를 붙인 말입니다. 낡은 것을 다시 손봐 새롭게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unrestrained merrymaking

examples.text: Sounds of revelry drifted from the square long after midnight on the eve of the festival.

origin.ko: revel('흥청대다')에 -ry가 붙은 말입니다. 떠들썩하게 놀며 즐기는 일입니다.

senses.en: regard with feelings of respect and reverence; consider hallowed or exalted or be in awe of

examples.text: Students revered the old professor, treating his every comment as a pearl of wisdom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 revereor('경외하다')에서 온 프랑스어 révérer에서 왔습니다. 두려울 만큼 높여 숭배한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: feeling or showing profound respect or veneration

examples.text: maintained a reverent silence

origin.ko: 라틴어 reverēns('공경하는')에서 왔으며 revere에 -ent가 붙은 말입니다. 깊은 경의를 품은 태도입니다.

senses.en: absentminded dreaming while awake

examples.text: The teacher's question broke into the student's reverie about the summer holidays.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 rêverie('몽상')에서 왔고 고대 프랑스어 resver('꿈꾸다, 헛소리하다')와 이어집니다.

senses.en: one who reviles

examples.text: The reviler of the new policy flooded the comment section with insults rather than arguments.

origin.ko: revile(욕하다)에 행위자 접미사 -er이 붙어 '욕하는 사람'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: intense aversion

examples.text: Readers expressed revulsion at the detailed descriptions of cruelty in the report.

origin.ko: 라틴어 revulsio에서 왔습니다. 몸을 '뒤로 확 잡아당기는' 반응이 강한 혐오감이 되었습니다.
